Intermediate representations connect task instructions to continuous actions in hierarchical robot learning. RT-H (Belkhale et al., 2024), Embodied Chain-of-Thought (Zawalski et al., 2024), and π0.5\pi_{0.5} (Physical Intelligence et al., 2025) use language motions, intermediate reasoning, or subtask prediction to guide action generation. Hi Robot (Shi et al., 2025), GR00T N1 (NVIDIA et al., 2025), and RoboBrain (Ji et al., 2025) separate high-level planning from low-level execution, while Cortex (Peng et al., 2026) uses canonical skills as its interface. Beyond control, REDS (Kim et al., 2025) and SARM (Chen et al., 2025c) use segmented demonstrations or subtask annotations to learn stage-aware rewards.
